How many signs place a child in a dehydration class?
Two or more signs in the same row.
What are the signs of severe dehydration?
Lethargic or unconscious, sunken eyes, drinking poorly or not at all, and a very slow skin pinch (more than 2 seconds).
What are the signs of some dehydration?
Restless and irritable, sunken eyes, drinking eagerly, and a slow skin pinch.
Where is the skin pinch done?
On the abdomen, halfway between the umbilicus and the side, in the long axis of the body, held for 1 second.

How much ORS is given after each stool in Plan A?
50–100 ml under 2 years; 100–200 ml at 2 years or more.

What is done if the child vomits during ORS?

How is Plan C given under 12 months?
30 ml/kg in 1 hour, then 70 ml/kg in 5 hours.
How is Plan C given at 12 months or older?
30 ml/kg in 30 minutes, then 70 ml/kg in 2½ hours.
What are the first signs that rehydration is working?
A stronger pulse, better consciousness and passing urine.
What are the signs of overhydration?
Puffy eyelids, fast breathing and crackles.
What are the complications of dehydration?
Shock, acute kidney injury, metabolic acidosis, hypokalaemia, sodium disorders with fits, hypoglycaemia and disseminated intravascular coagulation.
What are the criteria of severe acute malnutrition at 6–59 months?
A MUAC below 11.5 cm, a weight-for-height below −3 standard deviations, or bilateral pitting oedema.

Why are the signs of dehydration unreliable in severe acute malnutrition?
Loss of fat makes the skin pinch slow and the eyes sunken even without dehydration.
How is dehydration diagnosed in severe acute malnutrition?
By recent watery diarrhoea, a recent change in the eyes, thirst and reduced urine.
Which fluid is used for rehydration in severe acute malnutrition?
ReSoMal 5 ml/kg every 30 minutes for 2 hours, then 5–10 ml/kg per hour.
What is the only indication for intravenous fluid in severe acute malnutrition?

Why are standard ORS and Plan C not used in severe acute malnutrition?
